answer:
Configure a 2D transient, incompressible, laminar flow-past-a-cylinder case run with pimpleFoam.
Use the existing one-cell-thick mesh.
Change the 'frontAndBack' patches in constant/polyMesh/boundary to 'type empty;'.
Change the 'frontAndBack' entry in the 0/U file to 'type empty;' and remove the 'value uniform (0 0 0);' entry.
Apply 'type empty;' for 'frontAndBack' in all other field files such as 0/p.
The boundary types must match consistently between the boundary file and all field files.
Keep the inlet, outlet, and cylinderWall boundary conditions as already set appropriately for flow past a cylinder (fixedValue U at inlet, fixedValue p at outlet, zeroGradient p at inlet, noSlip or fixedValue (0 0 0) U on the cylinder).
Set the transport properties to U = 1 m/s at the inlet and nu = 0.01 m2/s, giving Re = 100 for a cylinder diameter of 1 m, a standard laminar benchmark with vortex shedding.
Set the simulation to laminar in constant/momentumTransport (or turbulenceProperties) with no turbulence model.
Set endTime to 300 and deltaT to 0.01 or smaller, adjusting maxCo and nOuterCorrectors in the PIMPLE dictionary as needed for stability.
Set writeInterval to 10 so several shedding cycles are captured with enough snapshots to observe the unsteady periodic behavior.
